reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain is a widespread and long-debated neuro-myth. Modern neuroscience has thoroughly debunked this concept. Neuroimaging technologies such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) scans show that virtually all parts of the brain are active throughout the day, even during sleep or simple tasks. Furthermore, if 90% of the brain were unused, damage to those "dormant" areas would have no impact on a person, yet in reality, damage to even minor areas of the brain can result in severe cognitive or physical deficits. Unused brain tissue also rapidly degenerates (atrophies), which does not happen in healthy brains.
